complete_compiler_story.headline: Client onboarding agents need governed case context

audience_fit.intended_user: Operations, compliance and relationship teams that coordinate document-heavy client onboarding across people and systems.
audience_fit.practical_action: Choose one onboarding case and record evidence, status, exceptions, decision history and the human owner before asking an agent to recommend a next step.
audience_fit.review_action: A named reviewer verifies every cited document, resolves exceptions, approves any consequential action and records the final decision separately from the agent recommendation.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A governed onboarding case file with versioned evidence, explicit exceptions, accountable approvals and measurable handoff times.

complete_compiler_story.summary: Databricks argues that wealth-management onboarding agents need a governed case context containing evidence, workflow state, exceptions and decision history. Its reference architecture coordinates specialized agents with human review and catalog controls, then measures the entire client journey. The design is vendor-authored guidance, not independent proof that the proposed stack improves outcomes.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Operations teams can pilot the pattern without adopting the full stack: preserve versioned evidence, assign each exception, require human approval for consequential steps and measure cycle time, rework and unresolved risk across the whole case.

complete_compiler_story.headline: A recommendation-audit Skill tests whether agents surface your work
complete_compiler_story.agent_skills_evidence: The first-party article reports 2,484 simulated recommendation sessions and concrete headline and description changes. This edition packages a distinct reusable procedure: define reader questions, run a fixed query set, record cited articles and omissions, revise only metadata, rerun the same set and require human review before publishing changes.

audience_fit.intended_user: Editors, knowledge managers and communications teams that need to test whether AI assistants can find and accurately describe published work.
audience_fit.practical_action: Define a fixed set of reader questions, record which articles an assistant recommends, revise only titles or descriptions, then rerun the same questions and compare results.
audience_fit.review_action: An editor checks every recommendation and omission against the original article, rejects misleading metadata and approves only changes that remain accurate for human readers.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A reusable recommendation-audit Skill with a frozen query set, before-and-after results, approved metadata changes, rejected variants and source links.

source.scope: Read the complete Every article, preserving its October 27 original date and November 1 update, 2,484 simulated sessions, test design, observed recommendation patterns, headline and description revisions, limits and distinction from live user traffic.
source.freshness_reason: The October 27 original date requires the 168-hour fallback. It is selected because the November 1 update supplies a distinct, measurable editorial procedure and simulation evidence not present in recent commitment-tally, parsing or release-control Skills.

read_evidence.scope: Read the complete Every article, preserving its October 27 original date and November 1 update, 2,484 simulated sessions, test design, observed recommendation patterns, headline and description revisions, limits and distinction from live user traffic.

complete_compiler_story.related_coverage: Turns a one-off discoverability experiment into a controlled editorial Skill with a fixed query set, source checks and reversible metadata changes.
complete_compiler_story.summary: Every reports 2,484 simulated sessions testing which articles AI assistants recommend, then describes headline and description changes intended to improve retrieval. The study is not live traffic and cannot establish general ranking effects. A reusable workflow freezes reader questions, records citations and omissions, changes metadata narrowly, reruns the same tests and preserves editorial review.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Editorial teams can distinguish discoverability from persuasion: hold the query set constant, compare before-and-after recommendations, verify every cited article and keep only metadata that remains accurate for people. The Skill produces evidence without promising traffic gains.
